name: _lazy_clone
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_lazy_clone(Tensor self) -> Tensor. Registered schema strings supplied for this operator: aten::_lazy_clone(Tensor self) -> Tensor. This representative overload is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest defines the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and tests must never be removed or the reference adapted to fit this single signature. Semantics: relocates the input's storage into a fresh tensor while preserving dense geometry (shape, strides, storage offset, dtype, device) and materializing any lazy conjugate/negative bit into the values; it is a CompositeExplicitAutograd storage op, not a view (result has _base None and _is_view() False, and for non-empty inputs its storage does not alias the input's storage), takes no scalar or broadcast operands, and passes a non-uniform upstream gradient through unchanged in backward for the non-complex dtypes the backward cases cover; for complex64/complex128 inputs that require grad the native operator raises RuntimeError("_lazy_clone does not support automatic differentiation for outputs with complex dtype.") at the forward call, so no complex gradient form exists. The only structural boundary is the empty tensor (empty inputs share the backend's single empty storage), and non-tensor or sparse-storage inputs raise errors owned by pytest. All behaviors above are exercised by the original pytest across value, layout/alias, storage-isolation, backward, special-value, empty, non-tensor-argument and sparse-storage cases; this definition encodes only the single representative signature.
